name: Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd
title: Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd - 543248 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: India SSSG 12.6% on traffic with no price hike; gross margin 70.8% targeted to 72% in 3 years, capex discipline, but no capacity or supply-side metrics beyond 80 stores/yr pace and Indonesia capex on hold.

capex.quote: we are not looking at putting in capex to grow restaurants, but we'll find ways to bring in efficiencies at current ADSs

triggers.label: SSSG 12.6%, highest in 15 quarters
triggers.quote: Same-store sales growth was 12.6%. This is the highest we have done in the last 15 quarters.

triggers.label: No strategic price increase taken
triggers.quote: We haven't taken any strategic price increase at all.

triggers.label: Gross margin 70.8% toward 72% target
triggers.quote: Our goal is, as we have outlined in the last call, is to get to 72% over the next 3 years.

triggers.label: Popeyes strategic options under review
triggers.quote: we are looking at all options on Popeyes

Our plan is to get to 72% in the next 2 to 3 years.
If you bring that down to 5%, 5.5 %, 5%, then yes, the growth -- the EBITDA at the restaurant level will go up by that much amount.

we are slightly ahead of where we thought we would be in terms of gross margin

red_flags.quote: Popeyes, like I told you, we are now in very deep conversations with the new promoters.

Once we have a steady plan put together that we are all fully energized and behind, then we will be in a position to share those plans.

summary.headline: India SSSG hit 12.6% in Q1 FY27 with revenue up 23.6% to INR682 crore and restaurant EBITDA of INR90 crore (13.2% margin).
summary.overview: Restaurant Brands Asia reported a strong Q1 FY27, led by India, where SSSG of 12.6% was driven by traffic rather than price, per management. India gross margin rose to 70.8% and company EBITDA more than doubled to INR52.7 crore. Indonesia remained loss-making at the Popeyes level but Burger King Indonesia reached positive restaurant EBITDA, with consolidated restaurant EBITDA of INR3.3 crore. A new promoter group has closed its stake acquisition, and management is working on a capital allocation plan for the next 3 to 5 years, with no details yet.

segments.name: Burger King India
segments.commentary: 590 restaurants (+71 YoY, +9 QoQ), 83% of group revenue; SSSG 12.6%, ADS INR1,31,000, gross margin 70.8%, restaurant EBITDA INR90 crore. Management targets around 80 net additions a year.

segments.name: Burger King Indonesia
segments.commentary: 137 restaurants (down from 179 after closing non-profitable units, per management), 15% of group revenue; ADS INR1,02,000, revenue INR124 crore, restaurant EBITDA INR6.4 crore. Bone-in chicken rose from about 30% to 50% of sales; self-ordering kiosks lifted average per check about 4-5%.

segments.name: Popeyes Indonesia
segments.commentary: 25 stores, 2% of group revenue; ADS about INR69,000, revenue INR15.7 crore, EBITDA loss INR3 crore. Management is in deep talks with new promoters and says strategic options, including exit, are not ruled out.

guidance_outlook: India gross margin target of 72% over the next 2-3 years (management said it is slightly ahead of plan at 70.8%).
India store growth pace of about 80 restaurants a year remains the goal.
Management said Q2 has started well, but it does not give forward guidance.
Indonesia: new value strategy expected to be in place by end-September; burger options in test in 3 markets since 1 July.
No new Indonesian restaurant builds planned this year; focus on rent reduction, solar, and a possible new broiler.
Franchisor RBI has committed USD9 million of marketing support to Indonesia over 3 years.
Management said a business plan and capital allocation plan for the next 3-5 years will come later; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: India expansion: 590 restaurants at 30 June 2026; target of about 80 net additions a year.
Indonesia: 137 Burger King and 25 Popeyes restaurants; portfolio cut by 42 restaurants over the past couple of years; no new builds planned in FY27.
Solar farm rollout across several India restaurants; new broiler installed that uses half the energy of the old one (management cited about 1-year payback in India).
Distribution clusters: management is building around distribution centres to lower primary and secondary transport costs.
demand_pricing: SSSG of 12.6% was traffic-led; management said no significant price increase was taken, only small price moves and some delivery changes.
Value strategy: 2-for-X offers (for example 2-for-99 and 2-for-79) remain the core of India's value positioning.
Premium and core menu: Korean and Peri-Peri burger promotions drove traffic; co-branded desserts and shakes contributed to growth.
Digital: about 90% of orders are digital; app and self-ordering kiosk data are to feed a CRM programme to launch soon.
Delivery profitability has improved; management said delivery mix rose on event-driven demand in some markets, not on competitor weakness.
Indonesia: the earlier 25,000 King Deal programme drove traffic but not enough volume; management said the 'missing link' is a new value strategy.

financial_highlights.change: highest in about 15 quarters per management

financial_highlights.value: loss of INR3.2 crore excluding forex; about INR12 crore loss including forex

financial_highlights.change: reduced 27% from loss of INR45 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR124 crore; ADS INR1,02,000; restaurant EBITDA INR6.4 crore (store EBITDA margin 5.2%)
INR15.7 crore; ADS about INR69,000; EBITDA loss INR3 crore

financial_highlights.change: seasonally high in Q1; management said it would fall to 5-5.5% over the year

qa_highlights.question: Break down the sharp SSSG increase into pricing, mix and volume; how will it play out for the rest of the year? Also, why did restaurant EBITDA not rise as strongly as SSSG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no significant price increase was taken; the 12.6% SSSG was driven by traffic, and Q2 has started well, though no forward guidance was given. Q1 marketing was 6.6% of revenue, seasonally high, and is expected to amortise to 5-5.5% over the year, which would lift restaurant EBITDA by that amount.

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG sustain at double-digit levels over the next 4-6 quarters, versus the earlier 5-7% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give forward-looking numbers; said the industry has turned positive after several muted quarters and that Q2 started very well.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new promoters' capital be deployed, and will there be further acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: This is the first call with the new promoters, the deal closed a few weeks ago, and a 3-5 year strategy covering capital allocation, growth rate, efficiencies and back-of-house integration is in progress. Plans will be shared once finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indonesia still on the twin path of fixing profitability or hiving off, and what is the Popeyes update?
qa_highlights.answer: Burger King Indonesia is improving and restaurants are EBITDA-positive. Popeyes is in deep talks with the new promoters; management said no strategic decision, including exit, is excluded and an update will follow once a visible path emerges.

qa_highlights.question: Delivery mix rose while peers reported different trends; is this due to lower competition? Also, why did head-office cost differ pre- and post-Ind AS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said delivery growth reflects profitable traffic and some event-driven demand in certain markets, not competitor weakness. CFO said the forex loss sits below EBITDA in finance cost and India G&A is INR37 crore, so it does not affect EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Will the promoters pledge more shares, and will they join future calls?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO declined to comment on promoter funding plans. CEO will discuss with the promoter Aayush Agrawal about joining a future call, but prefers to first finish the business plan.

qa_highlights.question: Indonesia capital needs, and how far does the Burger King Indonesia gross margin uplift from chicken mix go?
qa_highlights.answer: RBI has committed USD9 million of marketing support over 3 years; no new Indonesian restaurant builds are planned this year, with efficiencies targeted via rent cuts, solar and a possible new broiler. Chicken mix rose from about 30% to 50%, and management said rent was about 8% in Indonesia versus 12% in India at acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India gross margin target, and was there price-led help in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 72% gross margin target over 2-3 years, versus 70.8% now, which it called slightly ahead of plan. Gains came from distribution clusters around DCs and sourcing; no strategic price increase was taken, only small moves and some delivery changes.

risks_watch: Sustainability of 12.6% SSSG after a traffic-led quarter, given Q1 marketing at 6.6% of revenue and management's expectation that spend will fall to 5-5.5% over the year.

Indonesia: whether the new value strategy (targeted by end-September) and burger tests in 3 markets lift ADS; Burger King Indonesia restaurant EBITDA is only INR6.4 crore and Popeyes still loses INR3 crore per quarter.
Popeyes strategic decision, including a possible exit, is still open with no timeline beyond 'the next several weeks and months'.
Use and timing of new promoter capital: the 3-5 year capital allocation plan has no details; management said cash will fund growth of existing businesses and India and Indonesia will run separately.
Post-Ind AS India PAT is still negative (about INR12 crore loss including forex) and consolidated PAT is a loss of INR33 crore; forex exposure on Indonesia investments.
Rising delivery mix (44%) and the possible raw material inflation flagged by peers could pressure India gross margin despite the 72% target.
key_quotes: We haven't taken any significant pricing to have reached that 12.6%. It's driven by traffic that we have generated.
We are now in very deep conversations with the new promoters.

So we are very clear and focused to run these businesses as individual businesses, including the allocation of capital, which will go towards the growth of the business that we are currently operating.
Our goal is, as we have outlined in the last call, is to get to 72% over the next 3 years.
There are no -- there are absolutely no plans to consolidate those businesses there as far as we are concerned.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on India, citing record SSSG, margin expansion and a good start to Q2, but cautious on forward guidance and evasive on promoter funding, capital deployment and Popeyes, where management repeatedly deferred details until a plan is finalised.

adds.what: Burger King India net additions, about 80 restaurants a year (590 at 30 June 2026)

growth.why: Management targets about 80 India net restaurant additions a year (590 at 30 June 2026) and a 72% gross margin in 2-3 years (now 70.8%), with no revenue guidance; Q1 SSSG of 12.6% was traffic-led, but capacity is a stated plan and no orders or timed commitments back the store pipeline beyond the run-rate.

mgmt.note: A new promoter group has closed its stake acquisition and management is working on a 3-5 year capital allocation plan with no details or timeline yet.
